intro: In this lesson you'll describe a normal day in English, in order: first, then, after that. You'll also say when you do things: at 7, in the morning, every day. Warm-up: what time do you get up?
teachingNotes: This is a speaking lesson that puts known grammar to work: simple present for routines (he/she + -s), frequency words (usually, always) and at/on/in for time. Recycle them; don't re-teach them from zero.

Order words: First (the first thing), Then, After that, Finally (the last thing); Next is also fine if the learner uses it. They go at the start of the sentence; a comma after First / After that / Finally is common, after Then usually not. Encourage mixing then and after that instead of repeating one word.

Key common error: 'Every day I wake up at 5 and I am pray.' → 'Every day I wake up at 5 and pray.' Indonesian learners add am/is/are before an action word (*I am pray, *she is cook). With an action word there is no am/is/are. After 'and', say the person once (and pray) or repeat it (and I pray); with he/she the second verb keeps -s too (She gets up and prays).

Routine chunks: wake up (bangun, open your eyes) vs get up (bangun dari tempat tidur); have breakfast/lunch/dinner (have = makan here, not punya); have a shower (British) / take a shower (American) = mandi; go home (pulang) with no 'to' (*go to home), but go to work / go to school / go to bed with no 'the'.

Time expressions: at + clock time (at six, at half past five), in the morning/afternoon/evening but at night, on + day (on Saturdays = every Saturday), no at/on/in before every (*on every Sunday → every Sunday), from eight to four. Exact time before part of day: at seven in the evening (same order as 'jam tujuh malam'). Setengah enam = 5:30 = half past five, never 'half past six' (and British 'half six' = 6:30, so avoid it). 19.00 = seven p.m. / seven in the evening, not 'nineteen'.

Limits: present simple and frequency words only. No past simple (I got up), no future (I will / going to), no present continuous for the routine itself, no clauses with before/after + subject + verb (after I eat); 'after breakfast / after work' as chunks is fine. Keep sentences short and Indonesian contexts real (warung, kantor, ojek, KRL, masjid).

keyPoints.title: Your day in order: first, then, after that
keyPoints.explanation: Use the simple present and put the activities in order with First (the first thing), Then, After that and Finally (the last thing), at the start of each sentence. One person, two actions: join them with and and say the person once. Don't add am/is/are before an action word: I get up and pray, not 'and I am pray'.

examples.en: First, I get up and have a shower.
Then I have breakfast. After that, I go to work.
examples.id: Lalu saya sarapan. Setelah itu, saya berangkat kerja.

examples.en: Finally, I go to bed at ten.

id.title: Harimu secara berurutan: first, then, after that
id.explanation: Pakai simple present dan urutkan kegiatanmu dengan First (yang pertama), Then (lalu), After that (setelah itu) dan Finally (yang terakhir), di awal tiap kalimat. Satu orang, dua kegiatan: sambung dengan and dan sebut orangnya sekali saja. Jangan tambahkan am/is/are sebelum kata kegiatan: I get up and pray, bukan 'and I am pray'.

keyPoints.title: Saying when: at 7, in the morning, every day
keyPoints.explanation: at + a clock time (at six, at half past five). in the morning / afternoon / evening, but at night. on + a day (on Saturdays). No at/on/in before every: every day, every Friday. Careful: setengah enam is 5:30 = half past five.

examples.en: I get up at five in the morning.
We watch TV in the evening.
Bu Ani works from eight to four every day.
examples.id: Bu Ani bekerja dari jam delapan sampai jam empat setiap hari.

id.title: Menyebut waktu: at 7, in the morning, every day
id.explanation: at + jam (at six, at half past five). in the morning / afternoon / evening, tapi at night. on + nama hari (on Saturdays). Tidak ada at/on/in sebelum every: every day, every Friday. Hati-hati: setengah enam itu 5:30 = half past five.

assessment.prompt: Choose the correct answer. Choose the word for the first activity: '___, I close my warung. Then I have dinner. After that, I watch TV.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: First (Firstly is also fine). 'Finally' = 0 (it's for the last thing). 'Usually' or 'Every day' = 30 (true English, but they don't show the order).

assessment.prompt: Choose the correct answer. Correct the mistake: Every morning my mother gets up at five and she is cook rice.
assessment.rubric: Correct: remove 'is' and add -s: '... and (she) cooks rice'. Removing 'is' but writing 'cook' with no -s = 60. Keeping 'is' = 0.
options: every morning my mother gets up at five and cooks rice
Every morning my mother gets up at five and cook rice.
Every morning my mother gets up at five and she cooking rice.
assessment.correctOption: every morning my mother gets up at five and cooks rice

assessment.prompt: Choose the correct answer. Translate: Setelah itu, saya pulang.
assessment.rubric: Correct: After that, I go home. 'Then I go home' = 70 (good order word, but 'setelah itu' is after that). 'go to home' = 60. 'After that I am go home' = 30.
options: After that I go to home.

assessment.prompt: Choose the correct answer. Complete with in, on or at: I always drink coffee ___ the morning.
Choose the correct answer. Pak Budi says: 'Saya berangkat kerja jam setengah tujuh.' Complete in English with the time in words: I go to work at ___.
assessment.rubric: Correct: half past six / six thirty (6:30). 'half past seven' = 0 (that's 7:30, the Indonesian trap). 'half seven' = 0 (British for 7:30).

assessment.prompt: Choose the correct answer. Correct the mistake: I go jogging on every Sunday.
assessment.rubric: Correct: I go jogging every Sunday (no on before every). 'I go jogging on Sundays' is also correct. 'in every Sunday' or 'at every Sunday' = 0.

blocks.text:
A **routine** is what you do (almost) every day. You already know the tense for it: the **simple present** (*I get up, she gets up*). Most routine words are **chunks**: small groups of words you learn together, like one word. Learn them as they are:
- **have** breakfast / lunch / dinner: here *have* means **makan**, not *punya*.
- **go home** = pulang, with **no** *to*: 'go to home' is wrong. But it's go **to** work, go **to** school, go **to** bed (no *the*).
- **wake up** and **get up** are both *bangun*: you **wake up** when your eyes open, and you **get up** when you leave the bed.

id.text:
**Rutinitas** (routine) adalah hal yang kamu lakukan (hampir) setiap hari. Kamu sudah tahu bentuk kata kerjanya: **simple present** (*I get up, she gets up*). Kebanyakan kata rutinitas adalah **chunk**: kelompok kecil kata yang dipelajari bersama, seperti satu kata. Hafalkan apa adanya:
- **have** breakfast / lunch / dinner: di sini *have* artinya **makan**, bukan *punya*.
- **go home** = pulang, **tanpa** *to*: 'go to home' salah. Tapi go **to** work, go **to** school, go **to** bed (tanpa *the*).
- **wake up** dan **get up** sama-sama *bangun*: kamu **wake up** saat matamu terbuka, dan **get up** saat kamu turun dari tempat tidur.

rows.en: wake up
get up
have a shower

id.note: bahasa Inggris Amerika: take a shower

rows.en: get dressed
have breakfast
go to work / go to school
start work / finish work
have lunch
go home
cook dinner / have dinner
go to bed

blocks.text: With **he / she** (*my mother, Budi*) only the **first word** of the chunk takes -s: she **gets** up, he **has** breakfast (have → has is an exception), she **goes** home, he **watches** TV, she **finishes** work. The rest stays the same: 'she gets ups' is wrong.

id.text: Dengan **he / she** (*my mother, Budi*) hanya **kata pertama** chunk yang mendapat -s: she **gets** up, he **has** breakfast (have → has itu pengecualian), she **goes** home, he **watches** TV, she **finishes** work. Sisanya tetap: 'she gets ups' salah.

blocks.prompt: Rina finishes work at five and goes ___.
blocks.explain: Pulang is **go home**, with no *to*: home already includes the direction. 'at home' means *di rumah* (where you are), not where you go.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Rina finishes work at five and goes ___.
id.explain: Pulang adalah **go home**, tanpa *to*: kata home sudah berisi arahnya. 'at home' artinya *di rumah* (tempat kamu berada), bukan tempat yang kamu tuju.

blocks.text:
To tell your day **in order**, start each sentence with an **order word**:
- **First** = pertama-tama (the first thing you do)
- **Then** = lalu, kemudian
- **After that** = setelah itu
- **Finally** = terakhir (the last thing you do)
You'll also hear **Next** (berikutnya). Use **then** and **after that** in turns, so you don't say the same word every time. A comma after *First, After that* and *Finally* is common; after *Then* we usually don't write one.

You can also say **after** + a meal or work: *after breakfast* (setelah sarapan), *after work* (sepulang kerja).

id.text:
Untuk menceritakan harimu **secara berurutan**, mulai tiap kalimat dengan **kata urutan**:
- **First** = pertama-tama (hal pertama yang kamu lakukan)
- **Then** = lalu, kemudian
- **After that** = setelah itu
- **Finally** = terakhir (hal terakhir yang kamu lakukan)
Kamu juga akan mendengar **Next** (berikutnya). Pakai **then** dan **after that** bergantian, supaya tidak mengulang kata yang sama terus. Koma setelah *First, After that* dan *Finally* itu biasa; setelah *Then* biasanya tidak ditulis koma.

Kamu juga bisa bilang **after** + waktu makan atau kerja: *after breakfast* (setelah sarapan), *after work* (sepulang kerja).

rows.en: First, I get up and have a shower.
Then I have breakfast with my family.
After that, I go to work by ojek.
rows.id: Setelah itu, saya berangkat kerja naik ojek.

rows.en: After work, I go to the gym.
rows.id: Sepulang kerja, saya pergi ke gym.

rows.en: Finally, I go to bed at ten.

blocks.text: **One person, two actions? Join them with and.** Say the person once: *I get up **and** pray*. You may repeat it (*and I pray*), but **never add am/is/are** before an action word: 'Every day I wake up at 5 and **I am pray**' → **Every day I wake up at 5 and pray.** am/is/are is only for sentences with no action word (*I am tired*). With he/she, the second action takes -s too: *She gets up and **prays**.*

id.text: **Satu orang, dua kegiatan? Sambung dengan and.** Sebut orangnya sekali saja: *I get up **and** pray*. Boleh diulang (*and I pray*), tapi **jangan pernah menambahkan am/is/are** sebelum kata kegiatan: 'Every day I wake up at 5 and **I am pray**' → **Every day I wake up at 5 and pray.** am/is/are hanya untuk kalimat tanpa kata kegiatan (*I am tired*). Dengan he/she, kegiatan kedua juga mendapat -s: *She gets up and **prays**.*

blocks.prompt: First, I get up. ___ I have a shower. After that, I get dressed.
blocks.explain: It's the second thing, in the middle, so **Then**. *First* is already used for getting up, and *Finally* is only for the last thing.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: First, I get up. ___ I have a shower. After that, I get dressed.
id.explain: Ini kegiatan kedua, di tengah, jadi **Then**. *First* sudah dipakai untuk bangun, dan *Finally* hanya untuk kegiatan terakhir.

blocks.text:
You met these small words in earlier lessons. Here they are for your day:
- **at** + a clock time: *at six, at six o'clock, at half past five, at seven fifteen*
- **in the** morning / afternoon / evening, but **at night** (just remember this one)
- **on** + a day: *on Monday, on Saturdays* (with -s = every Saturday)
- **every** day / morning / Friday: **no** at, on or in before *every*
- **from** … **to** …: *I work from eight to four* (dari jam delapan sampai jam empat)
When you have a clock time and a part of the day, say the clock time first: *at seven in the evening*. That's the same order as Indonesian *jam tujuh malam*.
The time words usually go at the **end** of the sentence. You can also put them at the **start** to set the scene: *In the evening, I cook dinner.*

id.text:
Kata-kata kecil ini sudah kamu temui di pelajaran sebelumnya. Ini cara memakainya untuk harimu:
- **at** + jam: *at six, at six o'clock, at half past five, at seven fifteen*
- **in the** morning / afternoon / evening, tapi **at night** (yang ini hafalkan saja)
- **on** + nama hari: *on Monday, on Saturdays* (pakai -s = setiap hari Sabtu)
- **every** day / morning / Friday: **tidak ada** at, on atau in sebelum *every*
- **from** … **to** …: *I work from eight to four* (dari jam delapan sampai jam empat)
Kalau ada jam dan bagian hari, sebut jamnya dulu: *at seven in the evening*. Urutannya sama dengan bahasa Indonesia *jam tujuh malam*.
Keterangan waktu biasanya di **akhir** kalimat. Bisa juga di **awal** untuk membuka cerita: *In the evening, I cook dinner.*

rows.id: Pak Hasan membuka warungnya jam enam pagi.

rows.en: I usually have lunch at twelve.
rows.id: Saya biasanya makan siang jam dua belas.

rows.en: In the afternoon, the children play football.
rows.id: Siang/sore hari, anak-anak bermain sepak bola.

rows.en: My parents visit us on Saturdays.
rows.id: Orang tua saya mengunjungi kami setiap hari Sabtu.

rows.en: The street is quiet at night.
Sari walks to the market every morning.
rows.id: Sari berjalan kaki ke pasar setiap pagi.

blocks.text:
**The setengah trap.** *Setengah enam* is **5:30**, so in English it's **half past five** (half an hour past five), not 'half past six'. English counts from the hour that has passed, so take **one hour less** than the Indonesian number. Saying the numbers is always safe: *five thirty*. Avoid British *half six*: it means 6:30.

**Malam is two words.** **in the evening** = malam while you're awake (after about 6 p.m.); **at night** = when people sleep. And *19.00* in English is **seven p.m.** or **seven in the evening**, not 'nineteen'.

id.text:
**Jebakan setengah.** *Setengah enam* itu **5:30**, jadi dalam bahasa Inggris **half past five** (setengah jam lewat dari jam lima), bukan 'half past six'. Bahasa Inggris menghitung dari jam yang sudah lewat, jadi ambil **satu jam lebih kecil** dari angka Indonesianya. Menyebut angkanya selalu aman: *five thirty*. Hindari *half six* (bahasa Inggris Inggris): artinya 6:30.

**Malam itu dua kata.** **in the evening** = malam saat masih bangun (kira-kira setelah jam 6 sore); **at night** = saat orang tidur. Dan *19.00* dalam bahasa Inggris adalah **seven p.m.** atau **seven in the evening**, bukan 'nineteen'.

blocks.prompt: I go to the gym ___ Mondays and Thursdays.
blocks.explain: Monday and Thursday are days, and days take **on**. *on Mondays* (with -s) means every Monday.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: I go to the gym ___ Mondays and Thursdays.
id.explain: Monday dan Thursday adalah nama hari, dan nama hari memakai **on**. *on Mondays* (pakai -s) artinya setiap hari Senin.

material.title: Putting it together: a typical day

blocks.text: Here is a **typical day** (a normal day) for Sari, a nurse in Bandung. Look at three things: the **order words**, the **time words**, and the **-s** on every action, because Sari = she. Sari also uses **usually** from the lesson on frequency words.

id.text: Ini **hari biasa** (typical day) Sari, seorang perawat di Bandung. Perhatikan tiga hal: **kata urutan**, **keterangan waktu**, dan **-s** di setiap kegiatan, karena Sari = she. Sari juga memakai **usually** dari pelajaran kata frekuensi.

rows.en: Sari usually gets up at half past four.
rows.id: Sari biasanya bangun jam setengah lima.

rows.en: First, she prays and has a shower.
Then she has breakfast with her son.
rows.id: Lalu dia sarapan bersama anak laki-lakinya.

rows.en: After that, she goes to the hospital by motorbike.
rows.id: Setelah itu, dia berangkat ke rumah sakit naik motor.

rows.en: She works from seven to three.
rows.id: Dia bekerja dari jam tujuh sampai jam tiga.

rows.en: In the evening, she cooks dinner and watches TV.
rows.id: Malam hari, dia memasak makan malam dan menonton TV.

rows.en: Finally, she goes to bed at ten.

blocks.text: Now tell your own day in 5–6 short sentences: start with the time you get up, use **First, Then, After that** and **Finally**, and add a time word to most sentences. Keep it in the simple present: it's a day you have again and again, not one day in the past.

id.text: Sekarang ceritakan harimu sendiri dalam 5–6 kalimat pendek: mulai dari jam kamu bangun, pakai **First, Then, After that** dan **Finally**, dan tambahkan keterangan waktu di sebagian besar kalimat. Tetap pakai simple present: ini hari yang terjadi berulang-ulang, bukan satu hari di masa lalu.

blocks.prompt: Which sentence about Sari is correct?
options: She goes home and is rest.
blocks.explain: Sari = she, so both actions take **-s**: goes … and **rests**. *rest* is an action word, so there is no *is* before it.

id.prompt: Kalimat mana tentang Sari yang benar?
id.explain: Sari = she, jadi kedua kegiatan mendapat **-s**: goes … and **rests**. *rest* (beristirahat) adalah kata kegiatan, jadi tidak ada *is* sebelumnya.

assessment.dr-2: Pilih jawaban yang benar. Perbaiki kesalahannya: Every morning my mother gets up at five and she is cook rice.
assessment.dr-3: Pilih jawaban yang benar. Terjemahkan ke bahasa Inggris: Setelah itu, saya pulang.
assessment.dr-4: Pilih jawaban yang benar. Lengkapi dengan in, on atau at: I always drink coffee ___ the morning.
assessment.dr-5: Pilih jawaban yang benar. Pak Budi bilang: 'Saya berangkat kerja jam setengah tujuh.' Lengkapi dalam bahasa Inggris, Pilih jamnya dengan kata-kata: I go to work at ___.
assessment.dr-6: Pilih jawaban yang benar. Perbaiki kesalahannya: I go jogging on every Sunday.
